summary: Independent bridge audit found a second fail-closed gap beyond schema provenance: the semantic two-client evaluator validates entityCount/representedCount only as non-negative echoed identity fields and never ties them to canonicalEntityIds length. Its own passing fixture uses entityCount=20 and representedCount=20 with only two canonical entity IDs, and test_accepts_strong_two_client_evidence accepts that payload. The live client producer currently guards representedCount by waiting for exactly that many IDs, but evaluate_evidence.py is documented as the semantic PASS authority and should independently reject count/structure inconsistency rather than relying on producer behavior.
evidence: UNRENDERED-STUDIO-BRIDGE main tests/test_evaluate_evidence.py canonical_identity() sets entityCount=20 and representedCount=20 while passing_server(2) carries canonicalEntityIds=[world-entity:a, world-entity:b].
Current _require_server_evidence() checks identity equality and entity-ID equality but does not require representedCount/entityCount to equal canonicalEntityIds length.

Public PhysicsLabRealizer initial full-F2 realization creates every recipe entity, then syncMetrics sets registered entityCount and representedCount from the authoritative runtime/representation map, so the Hero Gate baseline has an independently checkable count/structure relationship.
